## Decide whether to factorise again

Start with the highest common factor. Then inspect the expression inside the bracket.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$12x^2-75$

::: {.fragment}

[Take out 3. What pattern remains?]{.annotation}

$=3(4x^2-25)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Identify two squares.]{.annotation}

$=3\big((2x)^2-5^2\big)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Keep the factor 3 outside.]{.annotation}

$=3(2x-5)(2x+5)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$12x^2-147$

Factorise fully. Expand your answer to check.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=3(4x^2-49)$

$=3(2x-7)(2x+7)$

Check: $3(4x^2-49)=12x^2-147$.

:::
